2. The brief facts of the case are as follows :
On 22-08-2018, the petitioner and her father had been to Krishnagiri for attending marriage in an Alto car bearing No. KA-51-M-4978.

On the same day at about 11:45 P.M., when they were returning from the marriage, on Bengaluru-Hosur road, near Balagaranahalli gate, the driver of Container Lorry bearing No. TN-28-BB-3445 drove the same in rash and negligent manner and dashed to the car of the petitioner.

Due to said impact, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries to her head, right hand,

Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.1,00,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 18% per annum.
3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondents No.1, 3 and 4 have appeared through their counsel and filed their separate written statements.
Whereas, the respondent No.2 did not choose to appear and remained absent.
Hence, the respondent No.2 is placed as ex-parte.
4. The respondent No.1 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.

It has admitted the issuance of insurance policy in respect of Container Lorry bearing No.
TN-28-BB-3445 and its validity as on the date of accident.
It seeks protection under Section 147 and 149 of Motor Vehicles Act.
It has contended that, the petition is bad for non compliance of provision under Sections 134(C) and 158(6) of Motor Vehicles Act.
The driver of the offending lorry was not holding valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident.
It has denied the occurrence of the accident and involvement of the offending lorry in the alleged accident.

It has contended that, the alleged accident was occurred due to negligence of the driver of the car bearing No. KA-51-M-4978 who herself hit the back side of the lorry and there was no negligence on the part of the driver of the lorry bearing No. TN-28-BB-3445.

It has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner,
injuries, medical expenses and treatment taken by her.
Further, it has sought for permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.2 as per Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
The compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
For the above denials and contentions, it prayed for dismissal of the petition.
5. Likewise, the respondent No.3 in his written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.
He has contended that, there is no negligence on the part of the driver of the Alto car bearing No. KA-51-M-4978.
The police after detail investigation have filed the charge-sheet against the driver of the container lorry (multi axle goods vehicle) bearing No. TN-28-BB-3445.
Further, he has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries, medical expenses and treatment taken by him.

It is further contended that, his car was insured with respondent No.4 and the insurance policy was valid as on the date of accident and his driver was having valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident and there is no contributory negligence on the part of the alto car.
The compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
For the above denials and contentions, he prayed for dismissal of the petition.

sentences.text: There is no evidence on record to show that, the accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of car bearing No. KA-51-M-4978 and not due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of Container Lorry bearing No. TN-28-BB-3445.

Further, the petitioner/P.W.1, has unequivocally denied the suggestion made by the learned counsel for respondent No.1 that, the alleged accident has not occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending container lorry bearing No. TN-28-BB-3445, but the same has occurred due to rash and negligent of the car bearing No. KA-51-M-4978.
Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.1 has cross-examined P.W.1 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from her mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of her evidence.

14. On meticulously going through the police documents marked as Ex.P.1 to 7, prima-facia it reveals that, on 22-08- 2018, at 11:45 P.M., on Bengaluru-Hosur road, near Balagaranahalli gate,
when the petitioner and her father were returning from Krishnagiri after attending marriage in an Alto car bearing No. KA-51-M-4978, the driver of container lorry bearing No. TN-28-BB-3445 drove the same in rash and negligent manner and dashed to the car of the petitioner.
Due to which, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries to her head, right hand, waist and other parts of the body.

The investigation officer has clearly stated in Ex.P.3 final report that, on the alleged date, time and place of accident, due to rash and negligent driving of the container lorry bearing Reg. No.
TN-28-BB-3445 the alleged accident has taken place and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries on the vital parts of her body.
15. Further, as per the Motor Vehicle Accident Report, which is marked as Ex.P.6, the accident was not caused due to any mechanical defects in the vehicle involved in the accident.

The rear right side wheel mudguard of container lorry bearing No. TN-28-BB-3445 is damaged and front bumber, left side head light, bonnet, front left side fender and front wind screen giass of car bearing No.
KA-51-M- 4978 are damaged.

When the accident was not caused due to any mechanical defects in the offending vehicle and as there is no evidence to show that, there was any negligence on the part of the driver of car, then it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending container lorry.

There is absolutely no rebuttal evidence placed on record by the respondents and even nothing is elicited in the cross- examination of P.W.1,
to show that, the said accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of car and not due to rash and negligent driving of driver of offending container lorry.
There is absolutely no reason to disbelieve oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.

Further,
as on the date of accident the driver of offending container lorry was holding a valid driving licence to drive the said vehicle.

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle, the place, date and time of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.

Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011) SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."

19. Therefore, for the above stated reasons and in the light of observations made in the above cited decisions, this Court is of the considered opinion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that,
she has sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident, occurred on 22-08-2018 at about 11.45 p.m., on Hosur-Bengaluru NH-7, near Balagaranahalli Gate, Anekal Taluk, Bengaluru District,
due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of container lorry bearing Reg. No. TN-28-BB-3445.

As per Ex.P.8 and 10 discharge summaries and Ex.P20 case sheet, the petitioner has taken treatment as inpatient for 13 days from 31-12- 2018 to 05-01-2019 and 23-08-2018 to 29-08-2018, in Sparsh Hospital, Bengaluru.
She might have spent considerable amount towards attendant charges during that period.

Therefore, compensation of Rs.1000 x 13 =
Rs.13,000/- is awarded towards the attendant charges.
v) Food and nourishment:

As per Ex.P.8 and 10 discharge summaries and Ex.P20 case sheet, the petitioner has taken treatment as inpatient for 13 days from 31-12- 2018 to 05-01-2019 and 23-08-2018 to 29-08-2018, in Sparsh Hospital, Bengaluru.
Therefore, compensation of Rs.800 x 13 = Rs.10,400/- is awarded towards food and nourishment charges.
vi) Conveyance expenses:

The petitioner has produced total eight receipts for sum of Rs.32,000/-,
issued by the Durga Ambulance Services, in order to show that, she has availed the ambulance service for conveyance to hospital.

But, on meticulous perusal of the said receipts, it reveals that, the date and serial number of bill mentioned in the said receipts are not in sequence and clearly seems to be manipulated and falsely created receipts.
Hence, the said receipts are not taken into consideration.

As per the evidence on record, the petitioner is the resident of Appanna Rao Street,
Krishnagiri Post, Krishnagiri District, the accident has taken place at Hosur-Bengaluru NH-7, near Balagaranahalli Gate, Anekal Taluk, Bengaluru District and she has taken treatment at Sparsh Hospital, Bengaluru.
Taking into consideration the distance in between all the above three places

,
compensation of Rs.4,000/- is awarded towards conveyance.

The petitioner has taken treatment for 13 days as in-patient at Sparsh Hospital, Bengaluru, for the grievous injuries sustained by her.
She might have taken rest for about 2 months and lost her income for the said period.

Therefore, Rs.12,500 x 2 =
Rs.25,000/- is awarded towards loss of income during treatment period.

It is evident from the documents placed on record that, as on the date of accident the age of the petitioner was 38 years and unfortunately she has suffered fracture of weight bearing bones i.e. left acetabular fracture with femur neck fracture and fracture of the right distal radius.
The evidence shows that, she has suffered permanent disability to the extent of 12% to the whole body.

The petitioner has deposed in her evidence that, till today she is under follow up treatment for the injuries sustained in the accident.
